kitName: TIA Studio Local-First Windows Desktop Blueprint
purpose: A reusable engineering brief for turning a local web application into a single-install Windows desktop application without depending on a hosted website at run time.
principles: Local-first: calculations, temporary working data and source files stay on the user's computer by default.
Deterministic domain engine: keep critical calculations in testable local modules, not in a generative-model prompt.
Production must not import development-only tooling such as Vite.
The desktop shell starts the bundled production server once, then opens localhost in Electron.
Treat raw customer files, credentials and legal evidence as confidential; do not commit, package or send them to external AI services.
Every release requires repeatable tests, a production build and a real-device installer test before it is described as validated.

runtimeFlow: Build the web client into dist/public.
Bundle the Node production entry point into dist/index.js.
Electron launches the bundled local server inside its main process or as an explicit child process.
Electron waits for a localhost health response on an allowed port range.
Electron opens a BrowserWindow to the local URL.
On quit, Electron stops the local server cleanly.

required: Serve static dist/public assets through a production-only server module.
Load Vite dynamically only when NODE_ENV is development.
Keep Vite and vite.config imports out of the production bundle.
productionBoundary.releaseGate: Fail the release if the bundled production server imports vite, createViteServer or vite.config.

releaseWorkflow.name: Verify production boundary
checks: Production bundle has no Vite import chain.
Desktop package configuration creates the intended targets.
No private source data or environment files are in the package.

releaseWorkflow.name: Package
targets: NSIS Setup for normal users and Start-menu integration
Portable executable as a fallback for restricted devices

releaseWorkflow.name: Smoke test
checks: The portable executable starts the local server and returns an HTTP response.
The Setup installer is tested on a real Windows device for install, Start-menu shortcut and launch.

releaseWorkflow.name: Handover
checks: Record version, SHA-256, test evidence and known limitations.
Commit source, docs and tests to a protected private repository.
Create a manual source handover package outside the project folder.

acceptanceCriteria: A Setup installation launches from Windows Start on a real Windows device.
The portable executable launches without network access after first download.
Production packaging does not require vite or other development dependencies at runtime.
The app clearly distinguishes local desktop access from controlled web-workspace access.
The release contains no raw customer schedules, spreadsheets, evidence files, secrets or credentials.
agentInstructions: Read the repository's existing packaging, test and security documentation before changing code.
Do not substitute a development server for the production server.
Do not claim Primavera parity, legal entitlement or an installer test that has not actually been run.
Write or update automated tests for production-import boundaries and packaging configuration.
Keep a changelog and a release manifest; do not silently overwrite older distributed artifacts.
inputsRequiredFromProjectOwner: Whether local-only use or controlled web collaboration is required.
Real-device test feedback for each installer target.
A decision on code-repository privacy and branch protection.
nonGoals: This blueprint is not a license-revocation system for already distributed local executables.
This blueprint does not provide code signing certificates or bypass Windows SmartScreen.
This blueprint does not move customer evidence into a repository or an external model.
